title: performance(canary): improve auto-detection with KV-aware hysteresis and rollout guards
author: Anika Shah
description:
Context: Our performance canary has been catching regressions, but we observed two recurring issues: 1) noisy signals for short-lived KV-cache churn which caused spurious rollbacks, and 2) oscillation when traffic splits changed rapidly during canary rollouts. This PR implements KV-aware hysteresis in detection logic and introduces rollout guard rules to avoid flip-flop deployments.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds KV-aware smoothing window: detector tracks per-model KV hit-rate and treats sudden KV cache churn as a separate signal to avoid attributing increased latency to model or infra regressions.
- Adds hysteresis thresholds to the latency/throughput detector so that a metric must cross the threshold for N consecutive windows (configurable) before triggering a fail.
- Introduces rollout guard layer: when a canary detects a regression, we now evaluate compatibility of fallback models, available capacity tiers, and recent autoscaling events before triggering an automated rollback.
- Adds configurable cooldown for automated rollbacks to prevent oscillation when multiple canaries are running in parallel.
- Adds end-to-end perf-canary CI job to validate hysteresis behavior with synthetic KV churn scenarios.

Checklist:
- [x] Detector: KV-aware smoothing implementation
- [x] Rollout guard: pre-rollback compatibility checks + cooldown
- [x] Tests: unit + integration perf scenarios
- [x] CI: perf-canary e2e job added to pipeline
- [x] Docs: perf-canary tuning guide updated

Why this approach: Prior versions used single-threshold checks which were too sensitive to transient caching artifacts. By separating KV signals and adding temporal hysteresis we reduce false positives while still detecting sustained regressions. The rollout guard prevents unsafe automated rollback when fallback paths are incompatible or autoscaling is already in progress.

Backward compatibility: All new parameters are optional and default to previous behavior (hysteresis windows default to 1, KV-awareness off by default). Operators can enable these features via the canary config map.

Related: ENG-1245 (perf canary improvements), ENG-1301 (rollout guard requirements), SUP-4421 (support case: repeated false rollbacks for customer X).

review_comments: Miguel Torres (2026-02-19): Suggest making the default hysteresis window 2 for safety — one-window defaults defeat the purpose. Also please add a perf budget test for the added overhead of KV tracking.

Anika Shah (2026-02-19): Responded: Default kept at 1 for backward compatibility; added operator note in docs and an example showing how to set to 2. Added a microbenchmark to CI to measure KV tracking overhead (results: ~0.6% median CPU).
Priya Patel (2026-02-20): Question on cooldown: what happens if cooldown overlaps with an ongoing autoscale event? Recommend checking recent scaling events before suppressing rollbacks.
Anika Shah (2026-02-20): Reply: rollout_guard now queries recent autoscaling events and will favor a delayed human-review if autoscaling is active; added a unit test for that scenario.
Liam O'Connor (2026-02-21): LGTM after nits. Left a nit on variable naming in detector.py (smoothed_latency -> smoothed_p95).
Anika Shah (2026-02-22): Fixed naming nits and pushed a small follow-up commit.

release_notes: Improved performance canary detection: added KV-aware smoothing, hysteresis windows to reduce false positives, and rollout guards with compatibility checks and cooldown to avoid oscillating rollbacks. Configurable via perf/canary/config_schema.yaml.
notes_for_ops: Defaults preserve previous behavior. To enable protections set perf_canary.kv_awareness=true and hysteresis_windows>=2. Suggested rollout: enable in staging for 48h, monitor perf-canary metrics dashboard and adjust thresholds. See docs/perf-canary.md for knobs.
qa_notes: Added synthetic KV churn scenarios covering short-lived churn vs sustained latency regressions. CI job 'perf-canary-e2e' must stay green. QA should run canary scenarios against staging clusters with representative KV hit distributions.
